name: Sallu
overview: Sallu was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin known primarily as the son of Meshullam. He lived in Jerusalem during the post-exilic period, as noted in the book of Nehemiah. His identification as Meshullam's son places him within the community of returned exiles residing in the city.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Sallu' means 'restored,' reflecting a possible theme of renewal or rebuilding consistent with the post-exilic context. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 11:7 and was not given directly by God but carries meaningful significance within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Sallu as the son of Meshullam, establishing his immediate family connection. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Sallu's significance lies in his representation of the faithful remnant from the tribe of Benjamin who resettled Jerusalem after the exile. His mention in Nehemiah underscores the restoration of the community and the reestablishment of the city under God's providence. As a resident of Jerusalem, Sallu embodies the fulfillment of God's promises to bring His people back to their land.
